newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-POLICE CHIEF WORRIED BY MILAN'S POOR FORM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLICE CHIEF WORRIED BY MILAN'S POOR FORM.

text.p: After two heavy defeats for A.C. Milan, local police are hoping for safety's sake that the Italian champions start to win again soon.
"If Milan carry on losing and the risks of protests increase, we will be forced to review policing at the stadium," Milan police chief Marcello Carnimeo said on Monday.
Angry Milan fans bombarded the San Siro pitch with flares and smoke bombs on Sunday after Milan lost 3-1 to city rivals Inter. They lost 6-1 to league leaders Juventus the weekend before.
Goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi was a particular target, his goal disappearing behind a cloud of smoke as irate fans reacted to Inter's third goal by hurling dozens of flares.
"If Milan carry on like that those sort of incidents could happen again and we must take counter-action," warned Carnimeo.
He said he was convinced the fans had organised their protests in advance and had smuggled the flares in at the last moment when security on the gates was less stringent.
Carnimeo said photographs and television footage of the crowd would be inspected and those fans identified as throwing flares would be banned from the stadium.
He defended police action, saying intervention during the match by police could have created dangerous confrontations with the fans.
Milan, 12th in the league and increasingly unlikely to appear in Europe next season, face the risk of a heavy fine and possible disciplinary action after Sunday's incidents.
